Description: A theme-aware web component that holds the host's content in a window, under a taskbar that brings the window's controls. The panel is part of the page's HTML when the page loads, and the host defines the five controls, then `task-bar`, then `window-panel`, each after loading its template.

template.description: The HTML template for the panel component.

div.window.description: The surface of the window. It holds the taskbar along its top and the content below it.

task-bar.description: The taskbar of the panel: the `task-bar` component, which brings the pin and the minimize, maximize, restore and close controls. The host defines the five controls, then `task-bar`, and loads their templates, before the panel. Cached as `elements.taskbar`: the panel listens to each control through it, with the control's own `on…` properties, so that connecting the panel again never subscribes twice, and hides the controls that do not fit its `condition`. The pin's `onpin` leads to the panel's `pin`, and its `onunpin` to `unpin`: the end user pins and unpins the panel by clicking the pin.

slot.title.description: The place where the title the host gives the panel is shown, in the centre of the taskbar. The host marks the title with `slot="title"`. The title is the host's own: the panel neither listens to it nor changes it.

div.content.description: The region below the taskbar. It holds the slot for the host's content.

slot.description: The place where the content the host places inside the panel is shown. The content is the host's own: the panel neither listens to it nor changes it.

condition.description: Indicates whether the window is normal, collapsed to its taskbar, or enlarged to fill the space it has. It decides which controls the taskbar shows: minimize and maximize while `normal`; restore and maximize while `minimized`; minimize and restore while `maximized`. Close is always shown. The pin is hidden while `maximized`, and shown otherwise, with the `status` the panel holds.

status.description: Indicates whether the window is pinned in place or unpinned. The panel holds it, and the pin in the taskbar shows it.

visibility.description: Indicates whether the panel is visible or hidden. A hidden panel is not shown and keeps everything else as it is: when it is shown again, it is as it was.

hide.description: Sets `visibility` to `hidden` and hides the panel.

show.description: Sets `visibility` to `visible` and shows the panel.

pin.description: Sets `status` to `pinned`, and the pin in the taskbar shows pinned.

unpin.description: Sets `status` to `unpinned`, and the pin in the taskbar shows unpinned.

parameters.description: Contains the new visibility of the panel.
